beginner_glossary.Neocloud / AI cloud: A cloud company built specifically to rent out AI computing (NVIDIA GPUs) at huge scale — unlike the general 'hyperscalers' (AWS, Azure, Google) that do everything. CoreWeave is the LARGEST pure-play neocloud; Nebius and IREN are smaller peers.
beginner_glossary.GPU: Graphics Processing Unit — NVIDIA's chip that does the heavy math for AI. CoreWeave buys these in enormous quantities (Ampere/A100, Hopper/H100/H200, Blackwell, and next-gen Vera Rubin) and rents the compute.
beginner_glossary.Revenue backlog: The total dollar value of contracts customers have SIGNED but CoreWeave hasn't delivered/recognized as revenue yet — a measure of future demand locked in. CoreWeave's backlog is nearly $100B (vs ~$6B of annual revenue), the core of the bull case.
beginner_glossary.ARR (Annualized Run-Rate Revenue): Recent revenue projected over a full year — a forward size gauge. CoreWeave targets $18–19B exit-2026 ARR and >$30B exit-2027 ARR (over 75% already contracted).
beginner_glossary.Active power vs contracted power (gigawa: Data-center size is measured in electrical power. 'ACTIVE' power = running and generating revenue (CoreWeave passed 1 GW). 'CONTRACTED' power = secured but not all online yet (>3.5 GW). The target is >8 GW active by 2030.
beginner_glossary.Adjusted EBITDA: A proxy for cash operating profit (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortization, and some items). CoreWeave's was $1.2B in Q1 2026 (56% margin) — strongly positive, unlike its GAAP net loss.
beginner_glossary.Adjusted operating income / margin: Operating profit after depreciation but before interest/tax (and excluding some items). This was just 1% in Q1 2026 (the 'trough') and is expected to rise to low double digits by Q4 — because new data centers cost money for ~2 months before they earn revenue.
beginner_glossary.Net loss (GAAP): The official bottom line. CoreWeave lost $740M in Q1 2026, mostly because of $536M of INTEREST EXPENSE (it funds its build-out with lots of debt) plus heavy depreciation.
beginner_glossary.CapEx (capital expenditure): Money spent building data centers and buying GPUs. CoreWeave guided $31–35B for 2026 — enormous relative to revenue, funded mostly by debt drawn as each site comes online.
beginner_glossary.Delayed Draw Term Loan (DDTL): A debt facility where CoreWeave only BORROWS the money as each data center is built and switched on — matching debt to revenue. Its DDTL 4.0 ($8.5B) was the first-ever INVESTMENT-GRADE (A-) loan backed by AI/HPC infrastructure, priced under 6%.
beginner_glossary.Investment-grade / non-recourse / weight: 'Investment-grade' = a high credit rating = cheaper borrowing. 'Non-recourse' = the debt is secured by specific assets/contracts, not the whole company. CoreWeave has cut its blended borrowing cost sharply (≈600bps from 2023–2025), a key advantage.
beginner_glossary.Inference vs training: TRAINING = teaching an AI model (huge, bursty compute). INFERENCE = running the finished model to answer queries (steadier, fast-growing). CoreWeave says inference is now >50% of its compute — a sign customers are monetizing AI.
beginner_glossary.Contribution margin: The profit a single deployment makes after its direct costs. New CoreWeave deployments run NEGATIVE for ~2 months (costs but no revenue), then normalize to the 'mid-20s' percent by month 3 — a timing effect, not a problem with the economics.
beginner_glossary.Foundation lab / AI-native: AI model developers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and AI-first startups. These were CoreWeave's original customers; they now represent LESS than 30% of backlog as enterprises diversify the base.
beginner_glossary.Self-build vs lease: CoreWeave gets data-center capacity two ways: LEASING space from data-center owners (fast) or SELF-BUILDING its own (more control + long-term upside). Its first self-build site comes online in 2026.
beginner_glossary.P/E vs revenue/backlog multiples: P/E (price ÷ earnings) doesn't work because CoreWeave is unprofitable. Investors instead value it on revenue, ARR, and backlog multiples, plus the path to profitability and free cash flow.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: CoreWeave is the largest pure-play 'neocloud' — an AI-specialized cloud that builds data centers, fills them with NVIDIA GPUs, and rents AI computing plus a growing software/storage/networking stack. In the AI/semiconductor supply chain it is a major CLOUD / NEOCLOUD node: one of the biggest buyers of NVIDIA accelerators (and a $2B NVIDIA equity investee), hosting the workloads of the world's leading AI labs and a fast-growing set of enterprises. Originally founded as a crypto-mining operation, it pivoted to GPU cloud and IPO'd in March 2025; it has scaled faster to $5B+ revenue than any cloud in history.
company_snapshot.headquarters: Livingston / Roseland, New Jersey, USA (≈50 data centers across the U.S. and expanding)
company_snapshot.founder_ceo: Co-founder & CEO: Michael Intrator. CFO: Nitin Agrawal. (Co-founded with Brian Venturo and Brannin McBee.)
company_snapshot.manufacturing_footprint: Operates ≈50 data centers; surpassed 1 GW of ACTIVE power and >3.5 GW of CONTRACTED power (targeting >1.7 GW active by end-2026 and >8 GW by 2030). Grows via long-term LEASES plus a new SELF-BUILD program (first self-build site online in 2026); no single data-center provider is >17% of active infrastructure. [Q1 2026 call 2026-05-07]

business_model.summary: CoreWeave makes money by renting AI computing at scale on long-term contracts. It signs multi-year deals with AI labs, hyperscalers, and enterprises (≈5-year average contract length), then raises debt and equity to build data centers and buy NVIDIA GPUs, and recognizes revenue as that capacity goes live. The flywheel: huge contracted BACKLOG (~$100B) → cheap, increasingly investment-grade financing tied to those contracts → rapid build-out → revenue and adjusted EBITDA → repeat. It is deliberately broadening from pure GPU rental into a full AI cloud stack (CPU, storage, networking, software) to deepen customer relationships and margins. The model is capital- and debt-intensive: strong adjusted EBITDA, but GAAP losses driven by interest and depreciation during hyper-growth.
how_they_make_money: GPU compute rental (the core): renting NVIDIA GPUs (Ampere→Hopper→Blackwell→Vera Rubin) for AI training and inference on multi-year contracts. [Q1 2026 call]

Integrated AI cloud platform: CPU, storage, networking, and software (incl. Weights & Biases) — each expected to exceed $100M ARR by end-2026; 90% of reserved-instance customers use 2+ products, 75% use 3+. [Q1 2026 call]

New consumption models & cross-cloud: Flex Reservation, Spot pricing, CoreWeave Interconnect (with Google Cloud), and CoreWeave Omni (running CoreWeave's stack in customers' own data centers) — widening wallet share. [Q1 2026 call]
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Scale + speed: the largest purpose-built AI cloud (>1 GW active, ≈50 data centers) with best-in-class 'dock-to-live' deployment times — turning scarce GPUs into revenue faster than rivals. [Q1 2026 call]

NVIDIA relationship: $2B NVIDIA equity, CoreWeave's software qualified as an NVIDIA reference architecture, early access to new GPUs, and a 5 GW opportunistic acceleration option — deep alignment with the key supplier. [Q1 2026 call]

Backlog + financing engine: a ~$100B contracted backlog underwrites the first-ever INVESTMENT-GRADE (A-) HPC-backed debt (<6%), structurally lowering cost of capital toward hyperscaler levels. [Q1 2026 call]
Full-stack platform + product attach: moving beyond GPUs into storage/networking/software raises switching costs and margins (high multi-product attach rates). [Q1 2026 call]
Customer roster: the world's leading AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Cohere) plus diversifying enterprises (Jane Street, HRT) — 10 customers committed $1B+. [Q1 2026 call]
ASSUMPTION-flavored: these are real edges, but the moat depends on continued cheap capital, NVIDIA's favor, and converting backlog to PROFITABLE (not just EBITDA-positive) revenue.

revenue_streams.analyst_view: CoreWeave's story is the gap between ~$6B of trailing revenue and a ~$100B contracted BACKLOG — multi-year demand already signed, including the world's top AI labs and a fast-growing enterprise/financial-services base. The crucial nuances: (1) it is diversifying away from its historical reliance on Microsoft (≈67% of 2025 revenue) — AI-native/foundation labs are now <30% of backlog; (2) it is broadening from raw GPUs into a stickier full-stack platform; and (3) inference (>50% of compute) signals customers are actually monetizing AI. The whole question is whether that backlog converts into PROFITABLE revenue while the company digests an enormous, debt-funded build-out.

competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: Versus other neoclouds, CoreWeave's edge is being FIRST and BIGGEST: the largest active power, the deepest NVIDIA integration (reference architecture), the most mature financing (investment-grade HPC debt), and the broadest full-stack platform. Versus the hyperscalers, it competes on AI specialization, speed, and being a neutral 'pure AI cloud' rather than a competitor to its customers' own businesses. Its disadvantages are balance-sheet leverage (heavy debt, GAAP losses), historical customer concentration (Microsoft), and dependence on continuous cheap capital and NVIDIA's favor. The competitive question is execution + financing durability, not whether AI-cloud demand exists.

financial_performance.analyst_view: CoreWeave is a study in hyper-growth vs. GAAP losses. The operating engine is powerful — revenue +112%, adjusted EBITDA $1.2B at a 56% margin, and a ~$100B backlog — but the company loses money on a GAAP basis because it funds a $31–35B/year build-out with heavy debt (interest expense $536M/quarter) and depreciates assets aggressively. Management is explicit that Q1 was the MARGIN TROUGH (1% adjusted operating margin) and that margins inflect to low double digits by Q4 as deployments mature. The bet: convert the backlog into profitable revenue, keep lowering the cost of capital (now investment-grade), and reach sustainable free cash flow — unproven, but the trajectory and contracted visibility are unusually strong.

It is priced as a hyper-growth, execution-dependent story, not on current profits.

valuation.analyst_view: CoreWeave is a high-conviction-on-both-sides AI-infrastructure stock. The bull case: the largest, fastest-growing neocloud with a ~$100B backlog, the top AI labs as customers, 56% adjusted-EBITDA margins, investment-grade financing, and a clear ARR ramp to >$30B by 2027 — at ~2x exit-2027 ARR. The bear case: it is GAAP-unprofitable, carries heavy debt (interest expense alone exceeds operating income), spends $31–35B/year, depends on continuous cheap capital and AI-capex staying strong, and historically leaned on one customer (Microsoft). The $36–$303 target range says it all: the debate is about LEVERAGE + the path to profit + AI-capex durability, not whether demand exists.

risks.why_it_matters: Heavy debt means huge interest expense ($536M/quarter, exceeding operating income); GAAP losses persist, and rising rates or tighter credit would hurt.
CoreWeave must continually raise tens of billions to fund $31–35B/year capex; any tightening of debt/equity markets would stall the build-out and backlog conversion.
Microsoft was ≈67% of 2025 revenue; while diversifying (Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, enterprises), heavy reliance on a few large counterparties remains a risk.
The whole model assumes AI compute demand keeps outstripping supply; an AI-capex digestion would hit utilization, pricing, and new bookings.
Backlog must convert into PROFITABLE, cash-generative revenue at targeted margins; build-out delays, component shortages, or labor constraints could pressure returns.
Roadmap, supply, financing, and even the cap table are tied to NVIDIA; any change in allocation, pricing, or strategy matters a lot.
Priced on forward revenue/ARR/backlog with a 52-week range of $63.80–$187 and a $36 analyst floor; any disappointment can cause large drawdowns.
If GPUs depreciate faster or older generations lose demand sooner than assumed, returns and asset values suffer (management argues older GPUs stay fully utilized).
AWS/Azure/Google/Oracle and Nebius/IREN/others compete for GPUs, power, customers, and capital; hyperscalers are also building their own AI capacity.
Equity raises and convertibles (used in the funding mix) can dilute shareholders, especially if the stock falls.

scenarios.disclaimer: Illustrative scenarios to frame the range of outcomes — NOT predictions, targets, or advice.

bull_case.thesis: AI demand keeps compounding, CoreWeave converts its ~$100B backlog into profitable revenue, margins inflect (Q1 trough → low double digits by Q4 → higher), cost of capital keeps falling (investment-grade), and it scales toward >8 GW by 2030 — becoming a durable, eventually cash-generative AI hyperscaler.
key_drivers: Backlog converts on schedule; exit-2027 ARR hits/exceeds >$30B; new bookings keep the flywheel turning.
Adjusted operating margin expands to low double digits and beyond; GAAP losses narrow toward profitability/FCF.
Investment-grade, contract-backed debt drives cost of capital toward hyperscaler levels; financing stays abundant.
Platform attach (storage/software/networking) + enterprise/inference diversification lift margins and reduce concentration.
bull_case.what_to_watch: Backlog conversion + ARR; margin inflection (Q2→Q3→Q4); cost-of-debt trend; customer diversification; free-cash-flow path.

base_case.thesis: Hyper-growth continues with improving but still-thin GAAP economics: CoreWeave hits its 2026 revenue/ARR targets, margins expand off the trough, financing stays available, and it remains the leading neocloud — but the stock stays volatile on leverage and profitability questions.
key_drivers: FY2026 revenue $12–13B and exit ARR $18–19B delivered; 2027 ARR ramps as contracted.
Adjusted operating margin reaches low double digits by Q4; GAAP losses persist but narrow relative to revenue.
Financing remains available at gradually lower cost; manageable dilution.
Stock tracks forward revenue/ARR multiples, swinging with AI sentiment.
base_case.what_to_watch: Quarterly margin progression; capex-vs-financing; customer mix; interest expense vs operating income.

bear_case.thesis: Capital tightens or AI-capex digests; heavy leverage and a $31–35B capex plan become a liability, backlog conversion slows or margins stay thin, and a GAAP-unprofitable, debt-laden stock de-rates sharply (analyst floor $36 implies deep downside).
key_drivers: Debt/equity markets tighten or rates rise; financing becomes scarce or expensive; the build-out stalls.
AI-capex pauses; utilization/pricing soften; bookings slow and backlog conversion disappoints.
Customer concentration or a large-contract change bites; competition pressures pricing.
Interest expense + depreciation keep GAAP losses large; the multiple compresses.
bear_case.what_to_watch: Any financing strain or rate increase; bookings/backlog deceleration; margin or ARR misses; AI-capex commentary; customer changes.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: CoreWeave (CRWV) is the largest pure-play 'neocloud' — an AI-specialized cloud that builds data centers, fills them with NVIDIA GPUs, and rents AI computing plus a growing full-stack platform — and the centerpiece of the neocloud trio alongside Nebius and IREN. It has scaled faster than any cloud in history: FY2025 revenue $5.13B (+168%) and Q1 2026 (reported 2026-05-07) revenue $2.1B (+112% YoY), with a 56% adjusted-EBITDA margin and a contracted revenue BACKLOG of ~$99.4B (the world's leading AI labs — OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Cohere — plus diversifying enterprises like Jane Street). But it is GAAP-UNPROFITABLE (Q1 net loss $740M, TTM loss $1.59B) because it funds a $31–35B/year build-out with heavy debt (interest expense $536M/quarter) and aggressive depreciation; management calls Q1 the margin TROUGH (1% adjusted operating margin) and guides to low double digits by Q4. The financing engine is the differentiator: >$20B raised YTD, including $2B NVIDIA equity and the first-ever investment-grade (A-) HPC-backed loan at <6%, structurally lowering its cost of capital. On valuation, the stock ($117, ~$63.85B market cap; IPO'd at $40 in March 2025, 52-week range $63.80–$187) trades at ~5x FY2026 revenue, ~3.4x exit-2026 ARR, and ~2x exit-2027 ARR (>$30B, already >75% contracted) — not extreme for triple-digit growth, but resting on converting backlog into PROFITABLE, cash-generative revenue. What is FACT is a dominant, hyper-growing, EBITDA-positive AI cloud with a ~$100B backlog and investment-grade financing; what is being PRICED is flawless execution and continued cheap capital while it digests enormous, debt-funded capex. The real debate is leverage + the path to GAAP profit + AI-capex durability (hence the $36–$303 analyst-target spread), not whether AI-cloud demand exists.
what_is_fact: FY2025: revenue $5.13B (+168%), net loss $1.17B (-$2.81), adjusted EBITDA $3.09B, backlog $66.8B; Microsoft ≈67% of 2025 revenue. [2026-02]
Q1 2026: revenue $2.1B (+112% YoY, +32% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA $1.2B (56% margin), adjusted operating income $21M (1%, the trough), net loss $740M (interest expense $536M). [2026-05-07]
Backlog $99.4B (~4x YoY); >$40B new bookings in Q1; 36% recognized in 24 months / 75% in 4 years; ≈5-yr avg contracts; AI-native/foundation labs <30% of backlog. [2026-05-07]
Power: >1 GW active, >3.5 GW contracted (+400 MW in Q1); targets >1.7 GW active by end-2026 and >8 GW by 2030. [2026-05-07]
Capital: >$20B debt+equity YTD incl. $2B NVIDIA equity and the first investment-grade (A-) HPC-backed DDTL 4.0 ($8.5B, <6%); no maturities until 2029 (ex self-amortizing). [2026-05-07]
Guidance: FY2026 revenue $12–13B, adjusted operating income $900M–1.1B, capex $31–35B, exit-2026 ARR $18–19B; exit-2027 ARR >$30B (>75% contracted). [2026-05-07]
Market (2026-06-15): price $117.03, market cap ~$63.85B, ~545.57M shares, 52-week range $63.80–$187.00, no dividend, GAAP-unprofitable (TTM revenue $6.23B / net loss $1.59B). [stockanalysis.com]
Analyst targets (36 analysts, 2026-06-15): 'Buy'; average $140.18, median $140, range $36–$303. [stockanalysis.com]
what_is_assumption_or_opinion: ASSUMPTION: the ~$100B backlog converts into revenue on schedule at the targeted mid-20s% unit contribution margins, and adjusted operating margin inflects to low double digits by Q4 2026.
ASSUMPTION: CoreWeave keeps lowering its cost of capital and funds $31–35B/year capex without crippling dilution or balance-sheet strain, eventually reaching GAAP profit / free cash flow.
OPINION: P/E is meaningless (GAAP losses); value on revenue/ARR/backlog multiples — and the dominant variables are LEVERAGE, profitability conversion, and AI-capex durability, not demand.
what_to_watch_next: Margin inflection: adjusted operating margin Q2 → Q3 → Q4 (toward low double digits) and the path to narrowing GAAP losses / free cash flow.
Backlog and bookings each quarter (conversion to revenue and ARR; exit-2026 $18–19B and exit-2027 >$30B targets).
FINANCING — cost of debt, new investment-grade facilities, NVIDIA support, and any dilution; interest expense vs operating income.
Customer diversification (reducing Microsoft reliance) and new $1B+ commitments; inference share of compute.
Capacity milestones (>1.7 GW active by end-2026; first self-build site) and component/supply-chain costs.
Competitive dynamics vs Nebius/IREN and the hyperscalers; AI-capex sentiment across the industry.
final_research_summary.no_recommendation_reminder: This report deliberately gives NO buy/sell/hold call. It lays out facts, assumptions, drivers, risks, and scenarios so the reader can form their own view.
